title: Introduce sampled-anchor snapshot gate for prompt-set regression detection
author: Arjun Khanna
description: Adds a new CI hook (sampled-anchor snapshot gate) that captures lightweight "snapshot" outputs for a small, fixed sample of prompts (anchors) and compares them across candidate model revisions to detect prompt-set regressions. Motivation: existing coarse SLOs miss subtle prompt regressions that only manifest on a small fraction of prompts; a sampled anchor approach provides a cheap, repeatable signal without running full evals. The PR includes: 1) an extensible gate implementation that computes multiple similarity metrics (token-level edit distance, normalized BLEU, and embedding cosine similarity) and aggregates them with configurable weights; 2) snapshot capture and storage integrations (S3-compatible snapshots with compact gzip+protobuf format); 3) a backfill utility to populate historical snapshots for a baseline set of anchors; 4) integration with the CI pipeline and smoke-eval runner so gates can be evaluated on PRs and nightly release candidates; 5) a small test harness and docs describing operator tuning. The gate supports: thresholded alerts, tolerant bucketing (per-cohort thresholds), and a resample-based flakiness attenuator that suppresses transient regressions by retrying the sample N times and requiring consistency. This description contains context, rationale, configuration knobs, and usage notes.
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial gate implementation and API (anchor snapshot object, comparator, and storage abstraction); add S3 snapshot writer and compact proto schema; backfill utility and CI workflow; tests and docs + threshold defaults and feature flag. release_notes: Added a sampled-anchor snapshot CI gate that provides low-cost per-prompt regression detection for prompt sets. Operators can enable the gate behind feature flag 'anchor_snapshot_gate' and configure snapshot storage, similarity weights, and cohort thresholds. Includes a backfill utility to generate historical baselines.
